title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
body_opening:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

### Decode MoE

Kimi-K3 decode defers MoE finalization so the consumer can fuse the final
top-k reduction. That changes the monolithic FlashInfer MoE output signature
from `(tokens, hidden)` to `(tokens, 0)`. The existing generic full-model
autotune dummy does not exercise this deferred-finalize path. FULL decode graph
capture therefore misses the `(B, 0)` cache entries, falls back to
`MoERunner tactic=-1`, and captures that default tactic into the serving graph.

their monolithic dispatcher under bounded token buckets. It tunes the actual
`(B, 0)` signatures without running the full
